16.speaker: Player
16.text: “Yes. It had its ups and downs but it was still fun.”

17.speaker: Ciara Walda
17.text: “And now we're growing old and bitter.”

18.speaker: Ciara Walda
18.text: “The usual story. A few friends dead, a couple of them missing after the coups. Oh, and I was almost arrested once.”

21.speaker: Ciara Walda
21.text: “Protesting against police brutality. Ironic, isn't it?”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “No good memories? You should try to be a bit more optimistic.”

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “We all went through tough times back then.”

24.speaker: Ciara Walda
24.text: “It's difficult when there's nothing positive about those times. Also, being a pessimist makes me realise the problems quicker.”

25.speaker: Ciara Walda
25.text: “Some of us more so than others.”

34.speaker: Ciara Walda
34.text: “I want to start off by saying this.”

35.speaker: Ciara Walda
35.text: “Unfortunately our fuel is running out at the Ministry of Education.”
35.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Maintain"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == true) == false)

39.speaker: Ciara Walda
39.text: “The state having had to rely on privatization funds is a disgrace. We are letting private interests meddle in the most essential service; learning.”

40.speaker: Ciara Walda
40.text: “It was very positive to see the administration dedicate the funding that was requested.”

44.speaker: Ciara Walda
44.text: “I want to thank you for allowing me to lead our education system in the right direction. By removing nationalist indoctrination and traditional teachings we have unlocked the potential of the next generation.”

48.speaker: Ciara Walda
48.text: “Although I insist that the funds are still necessary to close the gaps in services, I can't say we have been entirely off track.”

49.speaker: Ciara Walda
49.text: “I want to thank you for leading our education system in the right direction. Traditional teachings have long prevented proper progress.”

53.speaker: Ciara Walda
53.text: “What little money we allocated from privatization will be diverted to improvements.”

54.speaker: Ciara Walda
54.text: “I doubt it will be enough to make substantial change.”

58.speaker: Ciara Walda
58.text: “It comes at a welcome surprise in Sordish politics to see a President uphold their promises regarding education.”

59.speaker: Ciara Walda
59.text: “I am making sure that the additional funds are being used in the best way possible in order to resolve structural issues, speaking of.”

63.speaker: Ciara Walda
63.text: “Although you swore you would focus on education during your term, you have not lived up to that promise.”
63.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Maintain"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == true)

64.speaker: Ciara Walda
64.text: “Stagnation doesn't get anyone anywhere. Simply maintaining my ministry's funds got us sitting duck with the dozens of issues left unsolvable.”
64.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Maintain"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == true) == false)

68.speaker: Ciara Walda
68.text: “The effects of your decision are much greater than I think you realise. The real damage is being done to the younger generation.”

69.speaker: Ciara Walda
69.text: “I feel personally betrayed. You promised to focus on education during our term. And here we are suffering the consequences of a budget cut.”
69.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Maintain"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Education"] == true)

70.speaker: Ciara Walda
70.text: “I'm trying very hard to look past that but can't really.”

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: She regarded me coolly for a second.

72.speaker: Ciara Walda
72.text: “We had a once in a lifetime opportunity to eradicate the political indoctrination and the traditional methods of education. We have sadly missed this chance.”

73.speaker: Ciara Walda
73.text: “And as you have already stated, improving Sordland's sexist and horrendously outdated education system is low on your priorities list.”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “You played a huge part in this too, Ciara.”

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: She nodded and brought out a stack of papers from her bag.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: She nodded and brought out a stack of papers from her bag.

79.speaker: Player
79.text: “You played a huge part in this too, Ciara.”

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “There is nothing wrong with the current education system as it is.”

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: Her eyes widened, but she composed herself quickly.

87.speaker: Ciara Walda
87.text: “We've been through this. I showed you the statistics. Yet you didn't listen.”

88.speaker: Ciara Walda
88.text: “Never mind. There is no point talking about what's already done.”

89.speaker: Ciara Walda
89.text: “What priorities can there be other than the future of Sordland?”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “I am sure you will make do.”

93.speaker: Ciara Walda
93.text: “Never mind. There is no point talking about what is already done.”

94.speaker: Ciara Walda
94.text: “What other priorities there can be other than the future of Sordland?”

97.speaker: Ciara Walda
97.text: “That is precisely the problem. We can't.”

98.speaker: Ciara Walda
98.text: “We will have to make cuts from wherever we can.”

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: She brought out a stack of papers from her bag.

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: She brought out a stack of papers from her bag.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: Spinning her ballpoint pen, she went through the papers, organising some of them together.

109.speaker: Ciara Walda
109.text: “Our ministry has prepared the necessary framework regarding how to spend our increased education budget.”

110.speaker: Ciara Walda
110.text: “Our ministry has prepared the necessary framework regarding how to spend the funds we've gained through school privatization.”
110.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Maintain"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Privatization"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false)

111.speaker: Ciara Walda
111.text: “We can build new rural schools, improve the standards of existing ones, or increase salaries for all education workers."

116.speaker: Ciara Walda
116.text: “Because of the additional funds from privatization on top of the budget increase, we should be able to implement two of these options.”

117.speaker: Ciara Walda
117.text: “We have the capacity to implement only one of these options.”

130.speaker: Ciara Walda
130.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_PSnW_EducationInfo_Salary"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_PSnW_EducationInfo_Improve"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_PSnW_EducationInfo_Build"] == true) == false

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “Tell me about the plan to build new rural schools.”

132.speaker: Ciara Walda
132.text: “The issue is very critical, as we are losing many young people to ignorance and illiteracy.”

133.speaker: Ciara Walda
133.text: “Sordland's rural population is full of untapped potential. With enough education, these people could be an asset to our workforce and society."

134.speaker: Player
134.text: “Why should we increase the salaries of education workers?”

135.speaker: Ciara Walda
135.text: “The job itself should be held in higher regard and be compensated accordingly.”

136.speaker: Ciara Walda
136.text: “These are people who have chosen to dedicate themselves to the betterment of others. To helping raise the next generation.”

138.speaker: Ciara Walda
138.text: “Where to start? At the very least, they need new equipment and materials."

139.speaker: Ciara Walda
139.text: “Many of these schools are facing a shortage of desks and textbooks. The ones that aren't haven't been updated since before the Soll administration."

141.speaker: Player
141.text: “Let's move on to the decision and get on with it.”
141.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_PSnW_EducationInfo_Salary"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_PSnW_EducationInfo_Improve"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_PSnW_EducationInfo_Build"] == true) == false

142.speaker: Ciara Walda
142.text: “Look at how United Contana is pushing past Arcasia in education and research. It's because most of their rural populace has access to schools.”

143.speaker: Ciara Walda
143.text: “We ought to give them what they deserve.”

144.speaker: Ciara Walda
144.text: “If teachers lack the resources to give Sordish youth a proper education, it can be as bad as if they don't go to school at all."

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: She put the pen down and looked at me.

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “Build new rural schools. Our primary goal must be to increase access to education.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “Increase salaries of teachers, principals and other education staff all around the country.”

159.speaker: Ciara Walda
159.text: “That will definitely improve the education experience for our children.”

160.speaker: Player
160.text: “Improve rural education by purchasing new materials and upgrading old school equipment.”

163.speaker: Ciara Walda
163.text: “As I mentioned before, there are enough resources to initiate one more policy plan. What would your preference be?”

168.speaker: Ciara Walda
168.text: “It feels gratifying that we are finally serving the people directly. I will pass it down to the ministry.”

171.speaker: Ciara Walda
171.text: “Our teachers will be grateful. The payouts shall be prepared immediately.”

176.speaker: Ciara Walda
176.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Maintain"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Privatization"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Education_Budget_Increase"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EducationPrivatization"] == true) == false)

177.speaker: Narrator
177.text: Ciara put the papers back in her bag and left the meeting room.

180.speaker: Ciara Walda
180.text: “It's okay. Many of us have experienced similar stories.”

181.speaker: Ciara Walda
181.text: “I have talked with Ms. Suno to schedule some time to discuss the curriculum. She's a very astute woman, your secretary. You may want to consider promoting her."

183.speaker: Player
183.text: “Build new rural schools. Our primary goal must be to increase access to education.”

217.speaker: Ciara Walda
217.text: “The students of now will thank us in the future President Rayne. For we have unlocked the potential of critical thought this society desperately needed. In this way you have surpassed all the leaders before you.”

218.speaker: Ciara Walda
218.text: “It's a failure from my end to have come this far and not be able to make transformative change. We could have done so much more President Rayne. We didn't.”

220.speaker: Player
220.text: “It was not the right time and not the right choice Ciara.”

221.speaker: Player
221.text: “Sordland needs visionaries like you to reform to become something better.”

223.speaker: Ciara Walda
223.text: “I'm not going to lie. I'm doubting our strategy.”

224.speaker: Ciara Walda
224.text: “I am optimistic about the path that lies ahead of us now.”

228.speaker: Ciara Walda
228.text: “We are onto something promising and grand, Mr. President.”

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: She shook her head and brought out a stack of papers from her bag.

231.speaker: Ciara Walda
231.text: “My efforts of trying to reform the education system failed due to the lack of funding allocated to the Ministry.”

232.speaker: Ciara Walda
232.text: “Our education system is in shambles and I'm trying to do my best to pick up the pieces and keep it going.”

236.speaker: Ciara Walda
236.text: “A fact that the people will not forget.”

237.speaker: Ciara Walda
237.text: “New private schools are increasing the disparity of services in education. Lower-income households who can't afford the private school in their district and might need to send their children to a public school far away.”

246.speaker: Ciara Walda
246.text: “New private schools are increasing the disparity of services in education. Lower-income households who can't afford the private school in their district and might need to send their children to a public school far away.”

247.speaker: Ciara Walda
247.text: “The state having had to rely on privatization funds is a disgrace. We are letting private interests meddle in the most essential service; learning.”
